biology: Host recorded as plane tree (Platanus acerifolia).
soldier: The soldier has the head capsule yellowish brown tinged with red, mandibles purplish brown, labrum, antennae and pronotum yellowish brown, abdomen pale yellow, legs still paler, femora and tibiae pale yellow and tarsi rather yellow. Head capsule elongate-cylindrical, the sides roughly parallel, only slightly contracted at the middle, the posterior margin broadly rounded; in profile the dorsolateral angle of the frons hardly raised, the frontal slope about 45 degrees, the dorsal margin of the head nearly straight, the frontal surface flat, the Y-shaped suture discernible; compound eyes large and projecting, their distance to the antennal socket less than the short diameter of the eye. Labrum semicircular, the tips of the mandibles fine and curved, the left mandible about half the length of the head capsule. Antennae with 11–12 segments, the third shortest. Postmentum very long, about seven to eight times the width at the waist, widest in the anterior third, the waist region running parallel backwards from the middle. The width of the pronotum slightly greater than the widest part of the head capsule, the anterior margin with a broad shallow V-shaped concavity, the sides nearly parallel, the posterior margin projecting outwards with a shallow median notch, the median longitudinal line clear.
